To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a combination of negative wound therapy and punch‐grafting is superior to secondary intention healing or negative pressure wound therapy alone for wound closure after excision of melanoma on the sole of the foot.
a combination treatment using punch grafting and NPWT was superior to SIH and NPWT alone for post‐wide‐excision wounds on the foot.

a combination treatment with NPWT and punch‐grafting is an excellent treatment modality for post‐wide‐excision wounds on the foot, resulting in significantly shortened healing times, and favorable cosmetic outcomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the treatment of melanomas in dark‐skinned individuals.
the reconstruction of large wounds using the combination of negative pressure and punch grafting.
the development of new methods for the treatment of melanoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a combination treatment with punch grafting and negative pressure wound therapy is the most effective method for wound closure of post‐surgical excision of melanomas on the feet.

the combination treatment of NPDT and punch grafting can be a useful option to shorten the healing time and to improve the quality of the wound after wide excision in acral lentiginus melanomas of the foot.

punch grafting in combination with NPWT is an efficient treatment option with a high rate of success and a good cosmetic outcome, which is especially useful for patients who have limited mobility and/or a lack of a local skin pool.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a combination treatment with NPWT and punch‐grafting is a useful method to treat post‐wide excised wounds on the feet with favorable cosmetic outcome and significantly shortened healing time.
the combination therapy of NPWT and skin grafting is effective for wound healing after wide excision on the foot.
punch grafting with a negative pressure wound therapy system is a useful treatment for post‐wide‐excision wound healing on the foot.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of NPWT for fixation is a safe and effective way of performing punch grafting in the treatment of acral lentigines on the foot.
a combination of NPWT and a limited number of small punch grafts can be used to treat large wounds on the foot, after excision of melanomas in darker‐pigment individuals.
NPWT and punch‐grafting can be used to treat large defects on the foot after wide excision, with significantly shortened wound healing times and good cosmetic outcomes.
